Breath showing in great gold plumes, each one different, the longest hanging a full second before it thins away to violet.
A slow fall of birch seeds spiralling as they go, each one catching its own sliver of rose-coloured warmth on the way down.
Thistledown going past sideways in a tearing hurry, one seed snagged on a corner and spinning there like a held breath.
Luminous pollen drifting steadily upward through the whole frame, going the wrong direction entirely, an apricot haze that refuses to settle.
One cold gust combing every stem of moss flat at once, then releasing it all, a green wave breaking in reverse.
A column of midges dancing in one place with such commitment that their combined motion draws a trembling indigo smear in the air.
Frost crusting the rim in little upright needles, spreading inward one crystalline hair at a time, each needle catching turquoise from somewhere.
Mist lying far below like spilled milk, the very tips of the tallest firs poking up through it into clearer emerald air.
Air so still that a thread of smoke stands perfectly vertical for a long moment before losing its nerve and blooming sideways.
A fine ash-light drifting from nowhere in particular, each particle taking an extraordinarily long time to arrive anywhere, one speck gone gold mid-fall.
One big moth crossing at full speed, the slipstream behind it briefly parting the hanging pollen into two separate apricot curtains.
Dew beading so heavily that everything is sequinned, one bead grown so fat it wobbles, catches magenta, and finally lets go.
A faint warm updraught rising off the bark, carrying a single curled leaf in a long lazy spiral before setting it down again.
A single feather coming down end over end, tilting, correcting, tilting again, going nowhere fast in a very deliberate way.
The air so washed and clear it seems freshly wrung out, every distant shape arriving with an extra and unnecessary sharpness.
Thistledown snagged mid-crossing on an invisible current, holding perfectly still in moving air as though pinned by something too small to see.
A slow column of birch seeds all turning the same direction, a loose indigo helix unwinding into the warmer air below.
Breath hanging in great rose-lit volleys, the longer exhalations reaching further than expected and startling whoever breathes next into breathing more carefully.
A warm updraught arriving in sudden pulses, lifting everything loose a half-inch each time, a rhythm underneath the stillness like a slow heartbeat.
Pollen rising in a broad luminous column, gold thickening to amber at the centre where it crowds itself most, thinning again at the edge.
Frost needles spreading across a flat surface in a slow emerald-lit tide, the advancing edge moving fast enough to actually be watched.
Mist below stirring in one place as if something large moved through it, the disturbance spreading outward in slow violet rings.
One cold gust arriving from the north, tasting of high altitude and lichen, gone again before anyone agrees on what just happened.
A curl of smoke bending flat and then standing straight back up again, making its mind up twice, the second time more convincing.
Midges in their column briefly scattered by a breath of warm air, then reconvening in exactly the same spot with increased resolve.
